People who help you give you cards, and you never have to play them. A card makes a move easier, or lets you try a move at all, at the stops its help reaches. The party's cards stop working at the border.

Each turn, answer your phone, make up to one call, and then make one move. Police attention rises while the police search where you are, from low to rising to high. Once it is high, a police search where you are ends in a stop, and if it keeps climbing they stop you wherever you are. Each stop within 12 hours of the last one is worse, and the third step is house arrest. Get out of Costamaran airspace before the escape deadline, Tuesday at 2 p.m., which is 72 hours after the run starts.

The route and the people on it
Saturday, 2 p.m. You lost the election, and the court has barred you from leaving Valdória. Your second passport is in your coat.

Two unmarked cars sit outside the house in Portô Venla. The police run the departure inquiry for the Interior Ministry, and they are good at it. Rādiô Portô Venla has you on a yacht in the harbor, which is where you want the police looking.

Your brother or sister is abroad finding a jet, and no crew will book until they can say where it is going. A sponsor in another country will ask a ministry for your visa, for a price. Rosario Vélez, aide to Costamar's interior minister, can have people waiting at the border if Cerro Alto gets your name in time. Gianlūka Moretī runs the party. He can put a mayor, a judge, or a border post on the phone, and he writes down every call.

Nando has driven you for 11 years. Nonā Rosa Trentinī has a room in Nova Trentô, a phone, and a grandson who knows which boxcar the guards skip. Holt Greer works the midnight freight out of Salta and sells his chalk-marked crate to anyone with cash. Theo Bascom runs the yard. Two of the people helping you already work for the police, and which two changes every run.
The road

The road runs south through Pedra Branca, where the posts have not received the travel ban yet. It turns east to the colônia at Nova Trentô. Then it climbs to the rail town at Salta, where you board the midnight freight over the Huhūi passes. Three crossings lead into Costamar there, a day apart. One of them has taken Valdória's money, and you find out which when the sergeant walks into the hut with your passport and does not come back. Past the line is Portalba, a charter apron behind the port. A pilot there flies where the flight plan says.

A call takes hours, a move can fail, and police attention climbs while the police search where you are. Once it is high, a search where you are ends in a stop, and if it keeps climbing they stop you wherever you are. The other side

Before you start

The demo is one scripted escape in 20 steps with a coach beside you, and there is a shorter one for the government side. In the daily run everyone starts from the same draw, so you and a friend can compare endings. The game is one page that works offline once loaded, and it saves your run. It is hard on purpose, and one bad call on Saturday evening can end a run before it starts. A run takes 20 minutes, so when one ends you start another.
Valdória, Costamar, Altamira, Ardésia, and Nordavia are countries of the Nelosphere, Ron Bronson's fictional world, written since 1991, and the game's map places them on the real globe.
